baseline:
B
A sine wave is a continuous, periodic function that is inherently spread out in the time domain. In contrast, a square pulse is a transient event with a definite start and end, making it localized in time. This illustrates the time-frequency uncertainty principle: the sine wave is localized in frequency (one frequency) but not time, while the square pulse is localized in time but spread across many frequencies.

B
The Fourier Transform is a mathematical tool that decomposes a signal (represented in the time or spatial domain) into its constituent frequencies, thus converting it to the frequency domain.

B
This is a direct consequence of the Fourier Uncertainty Principle, which states that a function cannot be highly localized in both the time and frequency domains simultaneously. A larger spread (variance) in one domain implies a smaller spread in the other.

D
The uncertainty principle states there is a trade-off between localization in time and frequency. A signal that is very short and well-defined in time (like a cheetah's chirp) requires a wide range of frequencies to be created, meaning its frequency spread is wide.

B
This is a direct consequence of the time-frequency uncertainty principle, which states that a signal's duration and its bandwidth are inversely related; one cannot be minimized without increasing the other.
